Branch: mick/ltx2-qknorm-rope-vectorize (on main 02b983603d), commit 5dbb8589c1

## Motivation

`ltx2_qknorm_split_rope` (sm_100 path) runs 8 times per LTX-2 block. Its output pass reads x, the norm weight, cos and sin, and writes the output one bf16 element at a time. It is the largest non-GEMM kernel in the LTX-2 profile: 4.3 ms per stage-1 step for LTX-2, and 6.7 ms per forward for LTX-2.3 at batch 2.

## Modifications

`kda_kernels/csrc/diffusion/ltx2_qknorm_split_rope.cuh`: the output pass handles 8 consecutive RoPE pairs per thread with 16-byte loads and stores. It does so when the half head dim, the cos/sin strides and every base pointer allow; otherwise the scalar loop runs. The rstd reduction, the per-element math and the rounding are unchanged.

## Tests

`test_rope_ltx2.py::test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope_vectorized_matches_scalar`: the same inputs with cos/sin moved off a 16-byte boundary run the scalar loop, and both paths agree bitwise (d128 and d64, batch 1 and 2, odd sequence lengths). The existing exactness and alignment tests pass.

## Accuracy Tests

The new kernel is bitwise equal to the old one on 6 production shapes (B300). LTX-2 and LTX-2.3 MP4s of 4 requests each are byte-identical (measured together with the LTX-2.3 elementwise PR).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300, one q/k pair:

| shape (tokens q/k x heads x dim) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1536/1536 x 32 x 128 | 30.9 us | 16.6 us |
| 2x1536/1536 x 32 x 128 | 68.8 us | 36.5 us |
| 1536/126 x 32 x 64 | 14.0 us | 8.7 us |
| 2x126/126 x 32 x 64 | 10.1 us | 6.3 us |
| 6144/6144 x 16 x 128 | 69.8 us | 37.4 us |

LTX-2 stage-1 steps go from 48.3 ms to 47.2 ms (synced stage timing).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -342,6 +342,55 @@ def test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope_matches_torch_exactly(
     torch.testing.assert_close(k_out, k_ref, rtol=0, atol=BF16_FUSED_ATOL)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "batch,q_seq,k_seq,num_heads,head_dim",
+    [
+        (1, 7, 5, 32, 128),
+        (2, 4, 9, 32, 64),
+    ],
+)
+def test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope_vectorized_matches_scalar(
+    batch: int, q_seq: int, k_seq: int, num_heads: int, head_dim: int
+) -> None:
+    _require_b200()
+    torch.cuda.manual_seed(20261023)
+    hidden = num_heads * head_dim
+    q = torch.randn(batch, q_seq, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k = torch.randn(batch, k_seq, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    q_cos, q_sin = _ltx2_make_cos_sin(batch, q_seq, num_heads, head_dim)
+    k_cos, k_sin = _ltx2_make_cos_sin(batch, k_seq, num_heads, head_dim)
+    q_weight = torch.randn(hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_weight = torch.randn(hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    def misaligned(table: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # same values off a 16-byte boundary, which keeps the scalar loop
+        storage = torch.empty(table.numel() + 1, device="cuda", dtype=table.dtype)
+        copy = storage[1:].view(table.contiguous().shape)
+        copy.copy_(table)
+        return copy
+
+    def run(tables):
+        return ltx2_qknorm_split_rope_cuda(
+            q,
+            tables[0],
+            tables[1],
+            q_weight,
+            k,
+            tables[2],
+            tables[3],
+            k_weight,
+            eps=1e-6,
+            num_heads=num_heads,
+            head_dim=head_dim,
+        )
+
+    tables = (q_cos, q_sin, k_cos, k_sin)
+    vectorized = run(tables)
+    scalar = run(tuple(misaligned(t) for t in tables))
+    for actual, expected in zip(vectorized, scalar):
+        assert torch.equal(actual.view(torch.uint8), expected.view(torch.uint8))
+
+
 def test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope_rejects_unsupported_inputs() -> None:
     _require_b200()
     torch.cuda.manual_seed(20260630)
